themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber/Lyft/app-based cars) spiked to 15 complaints this week versus a baseline of 1.0 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1400% increase—suggesting a sudden surge in traffic congestion, illegal drop-offs, or safety incidents in Woodhaven/Richmond Hill.
evidence: 15 for-hire vehicle complaints this week vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 16.17)
1400% increase represents the sharpest spike across all monitored complaint categories
No prior news or community board discussion of this issue, suggesting it emerged rapidly
reporting_angles: Interview residents on specific streets seeing gridlock from app-based vehicles; map hotspots
Contact NYPD and TLC to understand enforcement response and whether permit caps have been reached

themes_detail.label: Street and Sidewalk Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 20 complaints this week compared to a 6.0 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 233% spike—pointing to a sudden escalation in outdoor disturbances or construction activity.
evidence: 20 noise complaints (street/sidewalk) this week vs. 6.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.42)
233% increase; this is the second-most-recent emerging spike after for-hire vehicles
Residential noise complaints (830 total over 90 days) show this is a baseline concern; street noise spike is a NEW acceleration
reporting_angles: Identify whether spike correlates with specific construction or street work permits filed with DOB
Canvass blocks with highest complaints to document source (bars, street vendors, vehicle noise, etc.)

themes_detail.label: Food Safety Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints rose to 7 this week from a baseline of 1.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 409% increase—suggesting possible new food vendors operating unsafely or inspections uncovering violations in the district.
evidence: 7 food establishment complaints this week vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.56)
409% increase; emerged this week alongside for-hire and noise spikes
311 data alone cannot identify which establishments or violation types; requires DOHMH inspection records to verify
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with DOHMH inspection records to identify which restaurants/vendors are involved and violation severity
Interview community board members about whether food cart licensing or street vending enforcement has changed

themes_detail.label: Rodent Complaints Acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 6 this week from a baseline of 1.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 300% increase—indicating a possible pest outbreak or sanitation failure.
evidence: 6 rodent complaints this week vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.02)
300% increase; one of several concurrent spikes this week
Community board budget requests include park safety and recreational programs but no explicit rodent/pest control emphasis
reporting_angles: Check DSNY sanitation enforcement records for missed pickups or litter violations on streets with rodent complaints
Interview residents about whether recent construction (315 DOB filings over 90 days) exposed rodent harborage

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints (Earlier Spike)
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 11 three weeks ago (vs. 1.4 baseline)—a 700% increase—indicating possible unlicensed dispensaries or public nuisance issues from legal retail operations.
evidence: 11 cannabis retailer complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.31)
700% increase; spike occurred 3 weeks ago, not this week—less urgent than current spikes but sustained concern
No follow-up data provided; unclear whether spike has subsided or remains elevated
reporting_angles: Interview CEEC (Cannabis Control Board) and local enforcement to determine how many licensed retailers opened in Woodhaven/Richmond Hill and when
Identify whether complaints relate to unlicensed operators or public nuisance (odor, loitering) from licensed shops
